title: Cohort Synthesis and Mixed‑Precision Onboarding Manual
author: Nadia Chen
body:
Summary

This document defines a reproducible process for synthesizing tenant cohorts, validating mixed‑precision (quantized) model variants for production, and integrating cohort‑aware evals and regression triage. It ties together: eval harness integration, prompt/benchmark selection per cohort, quantization profile safety checks, and an incident playbook for cohort‑level regressions. The goal is to reduce deployment risk when migrating live traffic to mixed‑precision model artifacts while preserving per‑tenant quality SLAs.

Scope and applicability

- Services: text-generation API (redwood-serve), chat routing (chat-proxy), and reranking service (ranker-core).
- Deployment modes: hosted API and Dedicated pools.
- Audience: model onboarding engineers, applied ML evaluators, SRE oncall, and solutions engineers running private deployments.

Definitions

- Cohort: a traffic slice grouped by stable attributes (tenant_id, primary_locale, average_context_length, feature_flags).
- Cohort fingerprint: fixed set of probes and telemetry that characterizes expected behavior for a cohort.
- Mixed‑precision onboarding: staged rollout of a quantized model variant (e.g., int8/float16 hybrid) with monitoring and fallback to fp32.

Why cohort synthesis matters

Large tenants and long‑tail tenants react differently to quant changes — some show embedding drift or function‑call instability. Cohort synthesis provides:

1) Representative probes for targeting high‑value regressions instead of global averages.
2) Efficient eval budgets by prioritizing cohorts with the largest cost/quality leverage.
3) Deterministic rollback triggers mapped to cohort‑level KPIs.

Cohort synthesis procedure (step‑by‑step)

1) Collect cohort candidates (data engineer / onboarding lead)
   1.1) Query 30 days of anonymized request metadata: tenant_id, model_id, avg_tokens, locale, function_call_rate.
   1.2) Compute candidate attributes: 95th percentile context length, mean response latency, embedding‑usage frequency.
   1.3) Flag cohorts with >0.5% global traffic share or those with prioritized SLAs.

2) Build cohort fingerprint (applied ML)\   2.1) Select 500–2,000 probe inputs per cohort using stratified sampling across intents and context lengths.
   2.2) Include three probe families: canonical_examples (deterministic intent), boundary_contexts (max tokens / truncated contexts), functioncall_scenarios (tool invocation templates).
   2.3) Label each probe with: probe_id, seed_context_hash, expected_response_anchor (text or structured).

3) Define acceptance criteria (product + SRE + applied ML)\   - Quality SLOs (per cohort): coherence_score >= 0.84 OR fall within 4% of baseline fp32 BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity anchor.
   - Latency SLO: P95 <= baseline_P95 + 40 ms for the same allocation tier.
   - Token cost delta: expected token cost <= baseline_token_cost * 0.95 (target) or <= 1.02 (upper bound).
   - Embedding drift threshold: average cosine shift <= 0.06 for embedding‑based similarity probes.

Eval harness integration checklist

- Create a cohort eval job in the eval orchestrator (eval-orch):
  - job_type: cohort_fingerprint_eval
  - model_variants: [fp32_reference, quant_int8_candidate, hybrid_fp16_int8]
  - probes: path/to/cohort/{{cohort_id}}/probes.jsonl
  - telemetry: capture tokens_per_response, kv_cache_hit_rate, function_call_success_rate, embedding_cosine_shift

- Configuration example (YAML):

  job:
    name: cohort-{{cohort_id}}-mixed-precision-eval
    targets: [fp32-ref, quant-candidate]
    probes_file: s3://eval-assets/cohort/{{cohort_id}}/probes.jsonl
    metrics:
      - name: coherence_score
        aggregator: mean
      - name: embedding_cosine_shift
        aggregator: mean
      - name: p95_latency_ms
        aggregator: percentile(95)

- Run schedule: daily for canary window (N=7 days), then hourly during ramp.

Prompt and benchmark guidance for cohorts

- Prompt families: aim for 3 canonical templates + 2 adversarial perturbations per intent.
- Budget: prioritize probes that cause stateful differences (long context continuation, multi‑turn referents).
- Benchmark metrics: coherence_score (human proxy model), instruction_adherence, factuality_sampler (precision@k), functioncall_correctness.

Quantization profile safety checks

Before any shadow or canary rollout, run this checklist:

1) Numeric stability sweep: run ten seeds on the eval harness and compare distributional metrics against fp32 reference (statistical significance test: two‑sample KS test, alpha=0.01).
2) KV cache compatibility: ensure candidate retains cache consistency across chunked streaming for contexts >8k tokens.
3) Function call determinism: for functioncall probes, verify structured output (JSON schema) matches reference for >=98% of probes.
4) Edge slices: test long‑token prompts (tail 1%) and high‑tooltip prompts (URLs/code) explicitly.

Quant tuning knobs to document per model

- layer_skip_threshold: string value (e.g., "top2-fp16")
- per_channel_scale: "true" | "false"
- clamp_strategy: "global" | "adaptive"
- fallback_policy: "immediate-rollout-hold" | "gradual-hedged-fallback"

Example JSON snippet to include in model manifest (store as string here):

{"model_id":"gptx-12b","quant_profiles":[{"name":"int8-hybrid","layer_skip_threshold":"top2-fp16","per_channel_scale":"true","notes":"optimized for long-context workloads"}]}

Staged rollout plan (operations)

1) Shadow validation: mirror 5% of cohort traffic to quant-candidate in shadow for 48–72 hours. No user-visible change. Telemetry: error_rate, coherence_score_delta, embedding_shift.
2) Micro‑canary: route 0.5% of cohort traffic to quant variant via canary route with immediate fallback to fp32 on per‑request failure. Ramp schedule: 0.5% -> 3% -> 10% over 24–72 hours if acceptance criteria met.
3) Mixed‑pool release: introduce quant nodes into dedicated pool at 10% capacity and measure cross‑tenant interference for 7 days.
4) Full cutover: proceed if P95 latency and embedding drift remain within acceptance.

Ownership and runbook triggers

- Owner: model_onboarding_team (primary), applied_ml_evals (secondary).
- SRE oncall notified when embedding_cosine_shift > 0.06 for any cohort OR coherence_score_drop > 0.05 absolute.
- Immediate actions on trigger:
  1) Pause ramp and revert canary routing via routing-control CLI: 
     rdc route update --route canary-{{cohort_id}} --action revert --reason "cohort-quality-trigger"
  2) Kick off Regression Triage runbook (steps below).

Regression triage runbook (cohort emphasis)

1) Triage owner assigned (applied_ml lead) and page created with: cohort_id, last_accepted_model, candidate_model, elapsed_ramp_time.
2) Automated bisect: run eval‑orchestrator bisect between fp32_ref and candidate, isolating by:
   - probe subfamily (functioncall vs long_context)
   - intent cluster (intent_id)
   - token‑budget bucket (short/medium/long)
3) Compare per‑probe diffs and prioritize top‑10 failing probes. Attach diff artifacts and topk embeddings shift table.
4) Hypothesis examples to test: 
   - "quant noise in early layers causing hallucination on multi‑turn referents"
   - "per_channel_scale mismatch for code blocks causing tokenization shifts"
5) Rapid mitigations: rollback, tighten fallback_policy, or apply targeted prompt rewrite for affected cohort.

Observability and dashboards

Minimum dashboard panels per cohort:
- Cohort traffic share (1h / 24h)
- Coherence score trend (baseline vs candidate)
- Embedding cosine shift distribution (boxplot)
- P95 latency by model variant
- Token cost delta and KV cache hit rate

Retention and audit

- Store every cohort eval job snapshot and probes.jsonl for 180 days in s3://eval-snapshots/{cohort_id}/.
- Keep a promotion ledger entry in model_registry: {model_id, cohort_id, timestamp, promotion_state, owner}.

Appendix A — Example probe JSONL line

{"probe_id":"c123-0001","input":"Summarize the following conversation...","expected_anchor":"Customer asked about refund policy; agent summarized steps"}

Appendix B — Quick CLI snippets

- Create cohort eval job:
  evalctl create job --type cohort_fingerprint_eval --cohort c123 --probes s3://eval-assets/cohort/c123/probes.jsonl --targets fp32-ref,quant-cand

- Pause canary route:
  rdc route update --route canary-c123 --action revert --reason "quality-trigger"

Appendix C — Decision log references

- Connected ADRs: decision record on hedged fallback routing (see /confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-hedged-fallback-2025).
- Model registry: see model_registry entry for specific quant profile names.

Notes and future work

- We plan to extend cohort synthesis to multi‑modal tenants (image prompts + text) and include embedding drift projections using temporal decay models.
- Investigate automated prompt rewrite templates as a mitigation baked into the canary route when drift is detected.
